title: Villages Plan
context: Should Vancouver turn 17 small commercial nodes into walkable, mixed-use neighbourhood hubs with more homes and shops?
argumentFor: Adds homes and everyday services in existing neighbourhood centres, making it easier to live near shops, jobs, and transit.
argumentAgainst: The scale and pace of change raised concerns about neighbourhood character, infrastructure, and whether the plan had enough public support.

source.name: City of Vancouver | Villages planning program

title: Renters Office
context: Should Vancouver fund a City-run office that helps renters understand their rights and navigate disputes?
argumentFor: Gives renters practical support in a tight housing market and makes tenant protections easier to understand and use.
argumentAgainst: The service cost roughly $600,000 a year and critics argued that tenant advocacy should be provided by senior governments or community groups.

source.name: City of Vancouver | Renter Office Newsletter

title: Safeway Towers
context: Should Vancouver approve three rental towers with more than 1,000 homes beside Commercial-Broadway Station?
argumentFor: Adds homes next to one of Vancouver's most connected transit nodes and keeps new housing close to shops and services.
argumentAgainst: The project's height, scale, affordability, and neighbourhood impacts drew major concerns, including the 'No Megatowers' campaign.

title: Beach Avenue Bike Lane
context: Should Vancouver maintain an all-ages-and-abilities bike route on Beach Avenue beside Stanley Park?
argumentFor: Protects a comfortable route for people biking and walking, including families, while reducing conflicts with fast-moving traffic.
argumentAgainst: Removing the lane would restore two-way vehicle traffic and give drivers more direct access through the Stanley Park edge.

source.name: City of Vancouver | Villages planning program

title: Natural Gas in New Builds
context: Should Vancouver allow new homes and buildings to use natural gas for heating and hot water?
argumentFor: Keeps more heating options available and may lower upfront costs for some new buildings and households.
argumentAgainst: Locks new buildings into fossil-fuel infrastructure and makes it harder to reduce emissions and meet climate targets.

source.name: City of Vancouver | Villages planning program

title: Bitcoin-Friendly City
context: Should Vancouver study using, holding, or accepting Bitcoin in city business?
argumentFor: Explores new payment and financial technology options and could position Vancouver as an innovation-friendly city.
argumentAgainst: Public money should not be exposed to a volatile asset, and studying Bitcoin may distract from more immediate city priorities.

source.name: City of Vancouver | Villages planning program

title: Abolishing the Park Board
context: Do you think Vancouver should replace its elected Park Board with parks governance directed by City Council?
argumentFor: Could simplify decision-making, reduce duplicated administration, and align parks with the rest of the city's services.
argumentAgainst: Removes a distinct elected voice for parks and recreation and concentrates more power over public spaces in City Council.

source.name: City of Vancouver | Villages planning program

title: Increasing Police Budgets
context: Should Vancouver spend more to expand the Vancouver Police Department, including funding for 100 additional officers?
argumentFor: Adds police capacity for emergency response, investigations, and public safety in a growing city.
argumentAgainst: Police increases take money from housing, mental-health, prevention, and community services that may address the causes of harm more directly.

source.name: City of Vancouver | Villages planning program

title: Zero-Means-Zero Budget
context: Are you in favour of freezing property taxes at the current rate, while requiring the City to find offsets and reduce or reshape programs?
argumentFor: Limits tax increases for households and businesses and pushes the City to find efficiencies before asking taxpayers for more.
argumentAgainst: A tax freeze can mean cuts to climate, housing, and other services while still increasing spending in areas such as policing.

source.name: City of Vancouver | Villages planning program

title: Downtown OPS
context: Should Vancouver allow a proposed overdose prevention site at 900 Helmcken Street?
argumentFor: Keeps people who use drugs alive and connects them with health care, treatment, and other supports in a high-need area.
argumentAgainst: Residents and businesses raised concerns about safety, street disorder, and whether the proposed location was appropriate for the surrounding community.

source.name: City of Vancouver | Villages planning program

title: Lower Speed Limits
context: Should Vancouver lower speed limits on some streets to reduce fatal crashes?
argumentFor: Lower speeds reduce the severity of crashes and make streets safer for people walking, biking, and rolling.
argumentAgainst: Lower limits can lengthen trips, frustrate drivers, and may have limited effect without better street design and enforcement.

source.name: City of Vancouver | Villages planning program
